ambiguities.description: Identification of Enrollment entity is implicit. The transcript does not explicitly state that enrollments have identifiers or what that identifier would be. We inferred an enrollment_id, but the business may expect enrollment to be identified by the composite key (Student, Offering), or another scheme. Does Enrollment need an independent EnrollmentId, or is the (Student, Offering) pair sufficient to uniquely identify an enrollment?

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings... a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Grade assignment timing and optionality. The transcript states 'At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.' It is unclear whether grades are mandatory (every enrollment must eventually receive a grade) or optional (an enrollment may not have a grade yet, especially during the semester). Also, it is unclear if a grade can be null/missing or if a missing grade is represented as a special value.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. The grade is one of A, B, C, D, or F.

ambiguities.description: Student enrollment capacity per semester. The transcript does not clarify whether a student can enroll in multiple offerings within the same semester or if there is a limit. Can a student take both Intro to Databases and Linear Algebra in the same semester?

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: Walk me through how enrollment works at the university... Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor.

ambiguities.description: Course offering uniqueness constraint. The transcript states that 'Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester,' and mentions that 'Intro to Databases might run in both Fall and Spring.' This implies that the same course can have multiple offerings in different semesters. However, it is unclear whether the same course can have multiple offerings in the same semester (e.g., two sections of CS101 in Fall 2026). Does a (Course, Semester) pair uniquely identify a single offering, or can there be multiple offerings per (Course, Semester)?

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: So the same course can have multiple offerings? Registrar: Right. Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester. Intro to Databases might run in both Fall and Spring.

ambiguities.description: Credit value range constraint. The transcript states that credit values are 'usually between 1 and 6.' This suggests a typical range but does not confirm whether this is a hard constraint or a guideline. Should a value_constraint be applied to CreditValue to restrict the range to [1, 6], or is this merely an observation that most courses fall in this range?

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.
